description: QSR: I am an individual contributor building a simple decision-support tool. Climate change makes seasons less predictable for farmers. Using NASA open data on rainfall, temperature, soil moisture and vegetation, it delivers clear, explainable crop-rotation recommendations for one region and a limited set of crops, showing the supporting data for each suggestion.
summary: FarmSky is a web tool that plans climate-smart crop rotations using 24 years of NASA rain data for three places in Kenya. You choose location, soil and priorities (water, soil or risk). It ranks three-season crop sequences and explains the scores clearly. The tool is a prototype for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 and works in five languages.
details:
FarmSky is a web tool that turns 24 years of NASA POWER rainfall and temperature data into practical crop rotation advice for three places in the Kenya highlands: Nyeri, Nakuru and Eldoret. Users choose their location, soil type and what matters most to them — saving water, protecting soil or spreading risk. The tool then ranks different three-season crop sequences and explains every score in clear steps. It also shows how the climate has changed, offers a 3D view of monthly rain, and lets users replay past years.

The main benefits are simplicity and transparency. Farmers and advisors can quickly see which rotations are more resilient in dry years, adjust the priorities to their own situation, and understand the reasons behind each recommendation. The tool works in five languages and offers both a simple and a more detailed view. It is free and runs in any modern browser.

The intended impact is to help smallholder farmers and agricultural advisors make better decisions under changing rainfall patterns. By making NASA Earth observation data easy to use, FarmSky supports more stable and climate-adapted farming in the region.

The project was built entirely with front-end web technologies: HTML, CSS and JavaScript. Three.js was used for the interactive 3D rain landscape. All climate data comes from the NASA POWER service. No special hardware or backend server is needed; everything runs directly in the browser.

FarmSky is creative because it does not only display climate data — it turns the data into ranked, adjustable advice that non-experts can understand and trust. The combination of transparent scoring, interactive visualisations and multi-language support makes complex satellite information more accessible.

When developing the tool, the team focused on real open data, clear explanations, honest limits, and ease of use. The goal was to create something practical for the NASA Space Apps Challenge that farmers and advisors could actually try and understand.
